summary: Two-part look at soaring US rents: Jeffrey Roper's RealPage rent-pricing algorithm, Sam Zell's real estate empire and his debt-fuelled wrecking of the Tribune Company, and Stephen Schwarzman's Blackstone buying up foreclosed homes after 2008.

evidence.note: critique of the zoning and NIMBY explanation pushed by developers and the press
Roper introduced as the first bastard; Alaska Airlines revenue manager in the 1980s
DOJ action over airline price-fixing software in the 1980s and early 1990s
Roper hired by RealPage in 2004 to build the YieldStar pricing system
RealPage buys rival LRO in 2017 despite antitrust review
Zell's birth to Polish Jewish refugee parents and Chicago childhood
Zell takes over the Tribune Company and installs shock-jock management
Tribune files for bankruptcy in December 2008 under Zell's leveraged deal
Zell's apartment holdings and spending against rent-control ballot measures
Schwarzman segment begins: childhood, Lehman Brothers, founding Blackstone
Blackstone buys foreclosed homes from 2011 and becomes a giant corporate landlord

notes: Survey of the 2022 rent surge rather than one biography. Primary subjects are the crisis itself plus Sam Zell, who titles part 2 and gets a full life story; Roper and Schwarzman have long segments but are secondary. Zell died in 2023, after airing. WWII-era rent control history and 1990s-2000s landlord murder cases are treated as illustrative background, not covered years. Covid eviction deaths get a couple of minutes only.
